What law or regulation currently in effect would work better as a general guideline?

I think a lot of traffic laws should not be an offense that can cause you to be ticketed but rather something that can be used to determine guilt or innocence in the event of an accident. If you think about it, 99+% of all instances of people speeding or not using their turn signal do not end up in a ticket. It cheapens the effect of the traffic laws in my view. Instead of protecting and serving, cops sit by the side of the highway and hope for someone to speed on by, or worse, find some poor schlep who has a headlight out - and of course this person is usually someone down on their luck, who might be having a hard time getting the money for a new headlight and now they have to pay for a ticket. The whole process turns cops into revenue generators part of the time, which is why my idea will never come to fruition of course.
I wish cops gave out vouchers for a new headlight from (insert auto parts store) instead.

I like your sentiment but I must respectfully disagree. I don't think it is Uncle Sam's job to subsidize people getting their car repaired. Plus this could start a slippery slope towards other repairs the government would be responsible for, with regards to everyone's car. If someone had a taillight out, rather than fix it, there would always be that guy who would just drive back and forth in front of a cop waiting to get a voucher.

Even if there was a system set up where license and registration fees went to pay for certain types of repairs and inspections (brakes, tail lights, etc), the system would be very much abused and we would end up subsidizing the least ethical of car repair shops.

The least cops could do is not give the offending driver one more thing to worry about with a $100+ ticket. To be fair, anecdotally a lot of times cops will let people off for offenses like this with just a warning.
